title: Conversation and run state
summary: Accepted tasks and native checkpoints retain collaborationmode independently of Agent Mode and Task Contract. Missing legacy values mean Default. Plan finalization stores canonical.

headings.title: Conversation presentation storage, search and paging
Rebuilding missing storage under a live owner

html:
Conversation and run state

Accepted tasks and native checkpoints retain collaboration_mode independently of Agent Mode and Task Contract. Missing legacy values mean Default. Plan finalization stores canonical Markdown with its SHA-256 digest, source identity and timestamp. Clean answers and compact artifact metadata survive in trace/chat history. The implementation action validates the source and atomically records card consumption, composer transition and normal task admission. Fresh implementation copies approved intent and preferences without transcript, receipts or a conversation handoff. These are additive JSON fields in existing state/settings stores; no migration is required.

Conversations retain user and assistant turns and link the run journal. RunStore owns dispatch claims, receipts, artifact links, jobs, wait events, amendments and checkpoints in the Server's RAM authority. The shared journal avoids copying the entire history into every run snapshot.

current_run/memory_state.py:StateDraft keeps transaction candidates private until commit. memory_store.py publishes a successful draft into the original owner containers, preserving the Activity references held by foreground workers. A replacement copy can strand a completion waiter even after a terminal receipt is stored. Failed transactions must leave those live objects unchanged. Immutable hub snapshots remain detached; preserving worker references does not allow a transaction to mutate published roots. See test_memory_native_execution.py and test_memory_run_store.py for the publication and recovery contracts.

Conversation presentation storage, search and paging

Visible chat history has a separate owner from the native execution journal. AgentConversationStore selects MemoryConversationStore for a registered Controller hub; unowned paths keep the standalone SQLite adapter. The RAM repository retains conversation metadata, user/assistant turns, attachments, compact visualization snapshots and accepted policy revisions. Reading a chat does not reconstruct native execution authority or authorize an operation.

Data ownership

flowchart TB W["Accepted history and metadata writers"] --> R["Conversation record transaction"] R --> C["Chat metadata and retained turns"] R --> I["Ordered navigation and turn indexes"] R --> S["Derived title, prompt and answer postings"] R -->|Deletion checks and note cleanup| K["Conversation KV owner and deletion fences"] C --> P["Checkpoint snapshot and recovery generation"] C --> D["Detached metadata or selected turn bodies"] I --> Q["Scoped history and navigation reads"] S --> Q Q --> D D --> U["API and browser presentation"]

ConversationRecords.changed updates navigation, per-conversation turn ordering, search postings and applicable retention indexes with the source-record mutation. Recovered authoritative rows rebuild the derived indexes. A streaming-only last_activity_at change does not rebuild navigation or search. Unpinning records the finished-task retention reset separately from semantic activity time.

Publishing a retained turn

sequenceDiagram participant W as History publisher participant S as Conversation store participant R as Record transaction participant H as Controller state hub participant C as Checkpoint worker participant D as Recovery generation W->>S: upsert_turn with request identity and retained result S->>S: Detach payloads and normalize presentation metrics S->>R: Begin atomic update R->>R: Recheck deletion, conversation and request ownership alt Deleted identity or required conversation missing R-->>S: Ignore late publication S-->>W: No retained turn added else Request belongs to another conversation R-->>S: RevisionConflict and rollback S-->>W: Ownership conflict else Eligible retained turn R->>R: Update chat, turn, indexes and retained-turn count R->>R: Prune oldest turns beyond the configured limit R->>H: Publish one immutable revision H-->>S: Committed RAM state S-->>W: Publication returns Note over H,D: RAM publication and completed disk save are distinct boundaries C->>H: Capture an immutable checkpoint snapshot C->>D: Write and publish the recovery generation end

A request cannot be moved to another conversation by updating its saved turn. Existing creation time and omitted attachments remain intact. Final-response outer whitespace is trimmed; internal text and formatting remain retained. Default capacity is 500 turns per conversation, configurable on the store. This bound is separate from pinning and automatic conversation/task expiry. Pruned turns also leave the derived search index.

When the native repository is installed, conversation deletion delegates to the conversation collector, which owns coordinated cleanup. Repository-only fixtures use one transaction for notes, turns and metadata. Deletion fences prevent late publication from recreating removed conversations. Neither deleting chat through this layer nor reading its saved output proves that every external effect has stopped; the collector's safety rules remain authoritative.

Reading bounded history

conversation_windows.py defines cursor encoding and the shared reply-order projection. Submitted order uses creation time plus request ID. latest_reply uses recorded activity/publication clocks and optional task lineage to group related attempts before selecting a page. It includes new requests and started replies, not just completed answers. A small disposable cache rebuilds when its header/lineage signature changes; it is not a second durable history store.

sequenceDiagram participant A as History API participant S as Conversation store participant R as Immutable record view participant L as Optional task lineage participant I as Reply-order index A->>S: Conversation, order, limit and one boundary S->>S: Validate cursor scope and clamp page size S->>R: Read metadata and ordering keys alt Submitted order R-->>S: Indexed creation-time and request-ID slice else Latest reply activity S->>L: Resolve task identities for compact headers L-->>S: Optional request-to-task relations S->>I: Header clocks, lineage and boundary I->>I: Rebuild changed ordering snapshot and select keys I-->>S: Selected request IDs and group metadata end S->>R: Read selected turn bodies and timing summaries S-->>A: Turns, count, older/newer/page cursors Note over A,R: No full trace restoration or model call

Only one before, after, through or around_request_id boundary is accepted. through includes its upper edge for remounting a previous page; continuation cursors remain strictly beyond the returned edges. Cursors bind to the conversation, excluded request and ordering mode. They are opaque navigation data, not access tokens. A missing conversation or requested anchor fails instead of selecting a different history.

Read or write boundary Default and limit
Retained turn capacity 500 per conversation by default; minimum configured capacity 1.
Turn window 12 by default, clamped to 1–32.
Compact conversation rail 250 by default, clamped to 1–500.
Search result page 50 by default, clamped to 1–200.
Search input At most 256 characters and the first 32 parsed word terms.
Explicit title edit Trimmed nonempty text, at most 160 characters.

Derived search

memory_conversation_search.py indexes titles and retained prompt/answer text. It case-folds Unicode word tokens and removes combining marks; words are intersected, rather than interpreted as executable query syntax. Relevance considers term frequency and document length, then retains the best matching turn per conversation. Simple recent navigation uses the ordered rail directly. Other sorts and filters select candidates before counting and paging, with request/conversation identities as stable tie-breakers.

Search cursors include the query/filter/sort fingerprint; reusing one for another selection is rejected. Running membership can be supplied by the management service from actual execution state. Search itself does not infer authority or execution from prose. Plain-text match excerpts are bounded, and full histories are not hydrated just to produce a page. Internal ids_only selection deliberately returns all matching identities and is not subject to the presentation page limit.

The RAM conversation fixtures cover immutable snapshots, concurrent publication, pruning, recovery and runtime SQL denial. Window fixtures cover tied timestamps, scoped cursors, reply/task grouping and selected-body reads. The RAM management contracts reuse search, ranking and filter cases with isolated state.

Run ownership and derived reads

The saved state dictionary is not itself permission to advance a run. A RunLease carries the exact lease identity and owner epoch outside the serializable checkpoint. Store writes validate that fence; a stale worker cannot regain authority by copying its state or by running in the same process. Claim rejection describes arbitration, such as an already-owned or superseded run, and does not by itself mean the task failed.

Journal scope resolves the conversation lineage separately from the visible chat. Existing bindings cannot be moved to another conversation or replaced with another journal identity. Reference-only runs use their continuation root; an ordinary independent request gets its own journal unless an authoritative inherited identity was supplied. Read paths require the recorded binding instead of reconstructing ownership from chat messages.

The native repository updates derived indexes in the same transaction as their source records. These are views of the accepted state, not independent execution owners:

Projection Contents and reader contract
Run history Creation cursors remain stable across checkpoints. Conversation pages return newest-first run identities; callers load details separately.
Artifact discovery Searches references, capability IDs and bounded public field names. Values and result bodies are excluded. Missing chats, absent source runs and tombstoned owners are skipped.
Attachment discovery Searches metadata for sources with retained conversation grants. Body files remain outside the index; missing-body filtering happens after the result limit, so a page may contain fewer matches than requested.
Gateway dependencies Tracks live run/request/task identities and selected Gateways for management and update admission. A live run without a Gateway still participates in Server draining.
Transfer recovery candidates Indexes unresolved transfer receipts. Bounded ancestry traversal includes older runs only for explicitly unknown operation IDs; selecting a candidate does not repeat its physical effect.
Capability outbox Preserves per-run event order through payload updates. Consumers read events after a cursor and own delivery acknowledgement.
UI queries Read conversation heads, watchdog state, artifact counts/revisions, amendment cursors and handoff history through the selected repository. These queries do not resume work or repair state.

Artifact and attachment discovery each accept queries of at most 256 characters and result limits from 1 to 50. Their substring matching folds ASCII letters to preserve the standalone SQLite behavior. Both require the native and conversation repositories to share one Controller hub, so deletion and grant checks observe a coherent snapshot. Discovery does not grant access to another conversation's content; explicit selection/linking performs its own authorization.

Permission amendment requires the run to remain unowned and waiting for the exact pending operation. A changed operation, an existing denial or an unsupported grant scope is rejected. A conversation grant updates the conversation policy revision and the run policy in one transaction. Failure before publication leaves both unchanged.

Stopped checkpoint protection retains late receipt facts, job status and unresolved effects while reapplying the committed Stop. It updates cleanup and lifecycle facts without accepting a stale worker's journal progression. A Stop acknowledgement therefore does not establish that every remote effect has finished or been undone.

The completion mailbox stores activity notifications with terminal receipt publication. Preparing a delivery selects up to 64 undelivered events and retains an in-flight delivery ID and sequence range. A retried decision receives that same batch. Consuming the batch validates the progression lease and advances only the matching delivery cursor in the decision's transaction. Receipt previews are attached after preparation commits; a missing result is presented as unavailable rather than inventing completion evidence.

The reconnect ledger is a UI projection in the native authority domain. Its explicit selected run is separate from progression ownership. When the selected row is absent, reads prefer unacknowledged active work, then pending work, then terminal history. Continuations can reuse one ledger identity, but an obsolete request ID cannot overwrite the current attempt. Acknowledging or deleting a ledger record changes UI history; these operations do not terminate a native run or erase its execution evidence.

Execution observation resolves retained run, request, task, Activity and job identities before presenting facts. Contradictory scope or tombstones produce a missing-result error; ambiguous matches require a more specific identity. Scheduler admission does not prove that a process started. Progress is recent only when evidence supports it, and a single inspection cannot prove stagnation. Native evidence uses a backend snapshot; supplemental scheduler, trace and phase reads are separate observations. The API does not probe a Gateway or repair execution during this read.

Lifecycle projection keeps semantic outcome, physical-work state and control eligibility separate. A completed child is not completion of a running task. Unresolved physical work can outlive a terminal display, and it prevents actions that require settlement. The compact presentation uses explicit field allowlists; expired OAuth interaction handling changes the returned copy rather than writing a replacement checkpoint.

Sequence manifests group exact Shell command receipts without copying their output. Publication requires the parent arguments, attempted-step count and each child command and receipt to agree. Inheritance links evidence to its original owner. Reading checks the source grant, retirement state, execution scope and every child link, then revalidates the manifest against the source invocation. A reference or digest alone grants neither execution authority nor permission to read another owner's evidence. Aggregate errors are read from the source journal and redacted at presentation.

These contracts have isolated fixtures in RAM interfaces, UI projections, run-state publication and Stop and metadata discovery.

Controller persistence

Ordinary aor serve and create_app acquire one fenced ControllerRuntimeStateHub before opening any state repository. All 15 first-party domains restore together; a partial domain graph cannot become ready. Immutable hash roots share unchanged state across transactions and checkpoint snapshots. Native state uses a binary snapshot adapter; other domains retain SQLite-backed recovery adapters. SQLite is also supported for explicitly compatible legacy native imports. Normal requests, misses and background execution cannot open or query Controller SQLite files. The Gateway owns a separate RAM execution authority, with its own resident limits, safety fences and checkpoint retention policy.

The runtime root defaults to controller-runtime beside the configured native-run database. Root and repository-path locks reject competing Servers, overlapping state paths and offline operations while the owner runs. HTTP worker counts other than one are rejected. aor run and aor chat send requests to the running Server.

checkpoints/manifest.json selects the committed recovery generation. One checkpoint is retained, with one temporary replacement while saving. Verified publication retires the old checkpoint and canonical .db import sources; those paths must not be used to inspect current state. Every domain in a selected generation must restore before the hub can become ready or write a checkpoint. There is no automatic rollback from a corrupt current generation.

/healthz includes runtime_persistence for the complete Controller graph. durability is pending until changes are checkpointed, current when the last confirmed commit covers the sampled RAM revision, or degraded after a checkpoint failure. has_uncheckpointed_changes explicitly reports changes that can be lost on a crash. uncheckpointed_revisions counts memory publications, not elapsed seconds or lost events. The last generation, owner epochs, checkpoint age, failure type and dirty age help diagnose persistence lag without reading SQLite or waiting for its writer. Availability can remain healthy while persistence is degraded. Health reports availability and persistence separately; it is not a release certification.

The Controller has no application memory budget, reserved-memory threshold, or memory-based task gate. The operating system controls memory allocation and exhaustion. Existing memory-budget options in older YAML files and environment variables are ignored. Health reports estimated state size and process RSS for observation only; a separate worker samples RSS once per second. These numbers do not delay or reject submissions. Actual allocation errors retain the normal error handling and transaction rollback. Checkpointing, idempotent replay, Stop, shutdown fences, and exclusive state ownership retain their existing behavior.

runtime.controller_checkpoint_cpu_fraction defaults to 0.25, overridden by AOR_CONTROLLER_CHECKPOINT_CPU_FRACTION. The checkpoint worker yields between rows after a 2 ms CPU quantum. This is cooperative pacing, not hard preemption of a single large serializer call. Automatic saves start only after two seconds without active task execution. HTTP traffic and ordinary RAM writes do not prevent idle saving. Explicit manual saves and final shutdown saves can also use runtime.controller_checkpoint_boost_cpu_fraction (default 1.0, environment AOR_CONTROLLER_CHECKPOINT_BOOST_CPU_FRACTION). The CPU boost delay is configurable as runtime.controller_checkpoint_idle_seconds / AOR_CONTROLLER_CHECKPOINT_IDLE_SECONDS. Set boost equal to the base fraction to keep constant pacing. A boost below the base does not reduce it. Activity is rechecked at each CPU quantum. Sleeping service threads retain their shutdown reservations without preventing an idle boost. Automatic snapshots have a 15-minute cooldown after each successful save finishes, configured by runtime.controller_checkpoint_cooldown_seconds or AOR_CONTROLLER_CHECKPOINT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (default 900; 0 disables the cooldown). Changes accumulate without moving the deadline. The first save after startup, manual Save, and shutdown bypass it; already-committed cleanup can finish without a new snapshot. Idle admission and serialization time can make recoverable state older than the cooldown. Retained cleanup items back off from 5 to 300 seconds after unchanged passes; committed evidence wakes them early. Unchanged passes do not rewrite journals or request saves. Maintenance telemetry distinguishes saving, cleanup, and waiting, with elapsed phase time; waiting is not active work. Failed attempts back off to at most 60 seconds; shutdown requests an immediate final attempt. Dirty bytes, checkpoint bytes, CPU/wall time, pacing and retry delay are exposed without probing disk on GET.

The checkpoint writer serializes each changed domain from the captured RAM snapshot. The native domain uses a data-only native-msgpack-v1 stream and an independent physical mirror; other domains use fresh SQLite files and matching JSON recovery bases. Native snapshots contain checked 256 KiB blocks, a complete-record footer and a catalog identity bound to the manifest. They do not deserialize executable Python objects. The writer never patches saved records using SQL deltas. Verified unchanged domains reuse immutable bytes; their baseline provenance is checked across process epochs. Genuine startup repairs are saved, while unchanged restored records remain clean. Migrations or incompatible loader transformations require a fresh dump of the affected domain.

The native adapter restores current binary snapshots without opening SQLite and rebuilds process-local index buckets. Supported legacy SQL/JSON native state upgrades on a subsequent save. The migration registry recognizes exact historical catalog fingerprints and fills declared additive column defaults while preserving existing values. Unknown catalogs and unsupported row layouts fail validation. Changing the generated catalog requires a version advance, registration of the previous fingerprint and declared migration defaults; the schema generator checks these conditions before writing its output.

A checkpoint remains a complete standalone generation, with format-specific integrity checks and fsync barriers. Replacement files have independent inodes. If one native copy is missing or damaged, recovery can use the verified mirror at the same selected revision and publish a repaired pair. It cannot substitute a different revision; if both copies are unusable, startup fails. Permission and other filesystem errors propagate rather than being treated as a damaged copy. Health retains the legacy incremental counters for API compatibility, with zero values; bytes encoded, reused, written, and elapsed time describe current save work. These boundaries are exercised by the binary persistence fixtures and catalog migration fixtures.

Before READY, the Server seals preexisting SQLite handles, collects startup cycles and freezes the surviving startup heap once. New request objects retain normal garbage collection; startup cycles remain until the last embedded Server closes. Their memory remains part of process RSS; the Controller has no memory-based admission budget. Disable this policy with runtime.controller_bootstrap_gc_freeze: false or AOR_CONTROLLER_BOOTSTRAP_GC_FREEZE=0. An embedding application that already froze its own heap must start the Server before freezing, because otherwise the SQL guard cannot inspect hidden old connections. GC thresholds stay unchanged.

A clean shutdown drains tracked background writers before a final checkpoint. If a writer outlives the shutdown deadline, the old process retains its owner lock until that writer exits and the final checkpoint attempt completes. A timeout or failure does not confirm durability, and repeated shutdown calls do not change that result into success. Startup restores the last committed generation; changes after it may be lost. Snapshot coalescing retains required trace events even when many progress updates share one checkpoint.

In-app /restart uses the same service teardown and final save before replacing the process, including when a restart callback is injected. It bypasses the automatic-save cooldown and waits for a fresh quiesced snapshot after any older save in progress. Concurrent restart requests share one operation. If the final save fails, the controller retains its RAM and exclusive ownership with new work disabled; another restart request retries saving without repeating service stops or gateway restarts. In-app /shutdown and /shutdownserver use the same final save and failure retention, then exit instead of replacing the process. /healthz.restart reports the operation (restart or shutdown) and draining, saving, restarting, stopped or failed, elapsed seconds, and a safe error message. The UI waits through draining and saving before starting its reconnect timeout and offers a retry when restart fails.

With the hub owner stopped, complete generations can be inspected or copied to a new, nonexistent destination using:

PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m agent_runtime.runtime_state.operator inspect /path/to/hub
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m agent_runtime.runtime_state.operator copy /path/to/hub /path/to/new-hub

The app keeps only the current checkpoint. --generation previous remains readable for older offline manifests that still contain an explicit previous entry. These commands verify checksums, acquire the owner lock and refuse an existing copy destination. New complete generations also retain registered context and generated-artifact bodies. Old generations without managed-file inventories remain metadata-only copies. Failures before manifest publication leave no committed manifest. A final directory-fsync failure can leave a complete visible copy whose durability is unconfirmed. Keep the source intact and choose a fresh destination on retry.

Checkpointed state can lag live memory. After a restart the last complete checkpoint supplies the saved permission policies, capability settings and Agent Check overrides. Global, conversation and prompt Allow settings remain allowed; Ask and Deny keep their usual behavior. Restarting does not add a confirmation. An interrupted save can lose changes made after the last complete checkpoint.

Pending permission prompts keep their identities, and checkpointed one-time permission approvals remain valid for the accepted operation until consumed or invalidated by a policy/target change. Ordinary permission approvals have no restart-specific or five-minute expiry. The separate unsafe-action challenges retain their existing expiration rules. Current capability restrictions still apply at dispatch. Invocation receipts and physical claims continue to prevent replaying uncertain effects.

The RAM continuation worker processes indexed affected runs and deadlines. When no work is ready it waits for publication or the next monotonic deadline; it does not scan retained history every half second. Expired time waits and Stop deadlines retain expiration facts across wall-clock rollback. Orphaned foreground claims use bounded per-run backoff, retain their claims through unavailable Gateway probes, and release only on matching physical completion evidence. Ready-queue removal does not itself grant progression authority. The worker rechecks deletion, ownership and Stop after reconciliation; the resume callback uses the normal claim path. Capacity subscriptions compare a dependency revision so a release racing the subscription cannot be lost. Timing diagnostics run after queue publication and cannot undo it if an observer fails.

Watchdog scheduling uses separate observation claims. An exact token reserves a watcher for 120 seconds; a matching retry release delays eligibility by 0.25 seconds. Forced observation bypasses only the ordinary due time, not another live claim, deletion or a completion-retry delay. Gateway inspection happens in the worker outside the RAM transaction. Starting an additional observer does not repeat bootstrap lease invalidation. These scheduling details are exercised by continuation fixtures and watchdog fixtures.

The shared watchdog evidence owner keeps completion probes separate from optional deep health samples. Stop makes cancellation confirmation due; it does not manufacture physical completion. Correlated terminal proof can settle resource claims without acquiring parent progression ownership. Observation errors preserve uncertainty and apply retry backoff. Attention incidents are tracked by reason and process identity, delivered in bounded redacted envelopes, and acknowledged by exact incident identity or the legacy generation/reason pair. This acknowledgement is separate from terminal receipt delivery through the completion mailbox.

Rejected-launch recovery is a narrow bootstrap repair for an older checkpoint-contention incident. It requires a stopped, unowned, untouched launch intent, its exact contention receipt and one correlated pre-dispatch rejection event. Missing Gateway jobs or generic failure text are insufficient. The repair republishes proven nonexecution through normal settlement; it never retries the command.

The default Server uses this worker; whole-system release evidence remains tracked in the closure ledger.

Restart recovery reloads state and reconciles pending dispatches and real jobs. A claim without a receipt remains unknown. Pending approval and credential requests stay bound to their originating operation and scope. Deleting a conversation respects tombstones and retention rules.

Current tool calls, receipts and references use operation_id, producer_operation_id and source_operation_id. Modes are conversation, agent and advisory; old input aliases are unsupported. Each SQLite owner checks its supported version before schema creation or recovery. Fresh databases create complete schemas directly; unsupported old databases are preserved and rejected with backup/fresh-directory remediation. The shared settings/EULA database has one version identity, as does the shared current/native-run database. Current native runs own an explicit journal index and capsule metadata; loads never infer old journal ownership or reconstruct native messages from chat turns.

The public core classes are RuntimeHost, AgentLoop, ToolCatalog, ExecutionEngine and RunStore. NativeModelClient, NativeExecutionConfig, directory names and compatibility wire fields are intentionally retained; they do not represent a second runtime.

The API/session wrapper is agent_runtime.api.runtime.engine.CompatibilityRuntime. The direct tool executor alone is named ExecutionEngine.

Retention clocks and output retirement

Conversation inactivity and task completion use distinct persisted clocks and derived ordered indexes:

Policy Clock and reset behavior Owner
Conversation expiry New owned semantic work/output advances last_activity_at; reads, heartbeats, replay and automatic cleanup do not. Unpinning keeps this clock. conversation_retention.py, auto_purge.py
Finished-task expiry Completion starts the clock; accepted resumed work clears it. The later of completion and the conversation's unpin-reset time starts the next countdown. task_retention.py, task_auto_purge.py

Both settings default off and accept positive integer hours/days. Each new record atomically captures an immutable auto_purge_policy_json snapshot; changes to defaults apply only to later creations. Off-created records remain exempt. Live switches pause acceptance without resetting saved clocks. Conversation defaults can import the older whole-day field. Invalid defaults cannot enroll new records; missing/invalid snapshots and unknown clocks remain protected. Bootstrap adopts missing legacy policies once from restored settings and persists them before workers start, retaining historical timestamps rather than restart time. Activity updates share the owning work's transaction, so a failed publication cannot leave a separate timer refresh. Source-context references do not establish conversation ownership.

Workers normally inspect at most 100 indexed candidates per page, every 60 seconds between passes, with a short yield between full pages. They advance past protected or failed candidates so an older protected entry cannot starve later history. A pause-switch change resets the scan cursor. Candidates are ordered by base expiry from the saved duration. Unpin extensions and enrolled tasks' longer retention periods are rechecked at acceptance; conversation countdowns show the effective deadline including these holds, even while task purging is paused. Exempt tasks add no hold. Projections are read-only and use the same deadline and protection evidence as acceptance; they are not deletion grants.

Acceptance rechecks the live switch, saved policy, pin state, age and unfinished work under the collector/task-launch guards. The collector's revision reservation rejects a snapshot invalidated by new work before journal I/O. Accepted deletion then owns its durable intent even if settings change afterward. Task deletion also protects unfinished dependency descendants and retained unknown physical effects; it uses the existing deletion service rather than an independent row-removal path. See Auto-purge settings for the user-facing controls.

Output retirement belongs to accepted deletion/expiry. It records exact run/job/Gateway cleanup targets without copying log bodies into the deletion journal. These identities survive an older checkpoint missing their RAM rows. Ordinary completion does not itself purge logs.

Remote cleanup requires settled execution and a matching output_purged, complete: true acknowledgement for the original job. Lost or unavailable replies retain retry identity and unresolved cleanup. Cancelled/lost jobs need separate ended/not-started liveness or an exited receipt before cleanup eligibility. The active collector's bounded observer pool owns remote waits.

Local scrubbing clears typed execution output and private previews while retaining outcome facts. It does not search-and-delete arbitrary matching user text. A live receipt link can protect shared backing output even while the deleted task's private copy is removed. Journal cleanup uses saved ownership ranges, and specialized trace/model-output repositories retire their own captures. Unknown legacy sharing stays protected rather than guessing a remote log owner.

Deletion queue lifecycle

The conversation/task collector separates accepted deletion, logical fencing, RAM collection and confirmed disk retirement. Acceptance writes an independent deletion journal before publishing its ownership fence. Overlapping requests keep their original deletion owners; new intent covers only newly selected identities. History can disappear while payloads remain queued for maintenance.

flowchart TD A[Persist exact deletion intent] --> B[Fence new work and late writes] B --> C[Discover ownership and install business tombstones] C --> D[Collect eligible payloads in idle slices] D --> E{Unresolved or shared evidence?} E -->|Yes| F[Retain exact owners and compact proof] F --> G[Observe accepted targets or changed ownership] G --> D E -->|No| H[Record collected epoch and revision] F --> H H --> I[Publish a verified covering checkpoint] I --> J[Retire safe obsolete files] J --> K{Exact revision still current and no unresolved work?} K -->|Yes| L[Acknowledge covered cleanup] K -->|No| F

The collector validates every repository collection against the closed retention ownership map. It follows run/request/task/continuation and grant relationships; a missing conversation alone cannot justify deleting an ambiguous run. New work and late staged commits are rejected by the published fences, while exact receipts for already accepted operations can still settle their claims. Deleted model leases and existing cancellation owners are signalled without resuming an Agent.

Background payload work waits for two idle seconds and uses 30-second windows starting no more often than every 900 seconds. Individual passes normally advance for 20 milliseconds between complete metadata units, and deletion batches contain at most 128 selected row identities. These are cooperative boundaries, not hard preemption inside a transaction. Active work pauses collection without extending the window. Unchanged retained evidence backs off from five seconds to five minutes; newly committed relevant evidence wakes the affected items early.

The live collector owns payload traversal. A checkpoint wakes that worker instead of competing for traversal or waiting for its next window. Offline/manual fixtures and drained shutdown can use the same cleanup coordinator synchronously when no collector thread is alive. Saving and cleanup completion remain separate results.

At most two outstanding observer/callback futures handle accepted remote targets and deferred transport invalidations. Cancellation and observation use retained Gateway context and exact operation identities. Missing targets, cancelled labels without physical proof and unknown historical effects stay unresolved. Sequence parents retain the completed child receipts needed to prove the aggregate closed; compact pending state removes user/output bodies while preserving settlement identity. No cleanup path retries the original command to discover its effects.

Independent tasks, schedules, monitors, context grants, pinned recipes and live receipt links can retain their backing data. A reference protects only its actual ownership scope, not permission for the deleted source to publish new private copies. Shared counts and unresolved-operation counts remain visible alongside RAM progress.

Physical retirement requires a verified checkpoint covering the collector's exact epoch/revision. Managed paths must belong to recognized roots, avoid symlink redirection and have no surviving owner. A settlement arriving during an older save cannot be acknowledged as covered by that older snapshot. Completion also requires no remaining unresolved operations; independently shared data stays retained. Durable completion markers and manifest acknowledgements must agree on restart; otherwise protection is restored first and collection resumes later. Legacy missing log ownership is retained as unresolved rather than guessed away.

Runtime purge and generation replacement

Runtime purge is an owner-requested maintenance operation, separate from normal conversation/task retention. It removes all runtime history, including pinned conversations, while preserving explicitly classified setup and reusable content. The storage manual owns the user instructions and offline commands.

flowchart TD A[Owner confirms exact phrase] --> B[Persist operation and target identities] B --> C[Drain work and confirm final Controller save] B --> G[Reconcile paired Gateway targets] C --> D[Restart into exclusive bootstrap ownership] D --> E[Stage and verify reusable setup and body references] E --> F[Publish replacement generation manifest] F --> H[Retire old history and restore inference setup] H --> I[Verify generation and record local completion] G --> J[Matching Gateway operation verifies and releases] I --> K{All targets complete?} J --> K K -->|No| L[Keep partial progress and fence unfinished targets] K -->|Yes| M[Record operation complete]

The coordinator persists the operation before beginning maintenance. Repeated acceptance returns an unfinished operation; the same submission ID also identifies its completed result. The target set includes disabled paired Gateways because they can still hold history. Preview reports estimates and failures; it does not prove that every preserved collection can be recovered. HTTP acceptance returns 202, not a completion claim.

The request handler does not remove local stores. It cancels active work, uses the shared shutdown owner and requires a confirmed final save before requesting a restart. A stopping timeout can trigger termination of verified owned native processes; it never permits racing a checkpoint writer. Once saving begins, the coordinator waits for that save. Failure leaves the Controller blocked for recovery.

Storage recovery runs before normal repository installation, with an exclusive owner, bootstrap phase and no loaded domains. A journal records fixed store-path bindings, prepared generation, publication/deletion progress and per-target receipts. Acceptance and the offline CLI reject pending relocation; recovery rejects changed store paths while a purge is unfinished.

The closed inventory classifies each domain, table and managed root. New unclassified storage blocks deletion. Preparation reads only preserved/mixed collections and validates their schemas; missing or corrupt committed setup is an error. The independently checksummed native setup sidecar allows disposable native snapshot corruption to be bypassed without inventing replacement configuration.

Field adapters detach known execution provenance and observations while retaining authored values. Active or paused recurring schedules advance to eligible future occurrences; expired one-time schedules complete. Saved monitors keep their definitions, while transient model-led monitors are discarded. Previously running saved monitors become queued; their retained IDs allow the online coordinator to resume them when required Gateways are ready. Paused monitors stay paused.

Reusable definitions can retain context/artifact IDs and workflow asset hashes. Preparation verifies the required bodies and records their ownership. Context grants from old conversations are removed; retained artifacts move into detached managed workspaces. The operation selectively keeps those live bodies rather than staging duplicate payload contents. Unreferenced managed bodies are removed.

Before deletion, recovery verifies prepared stores and walks every deletion root. It then publishes the new manifest, retires old generations and history, restores sanitized inference setup, and verifies the replacement and retained bodies. Local completion is durable before temporary preparation descriptors are removed. The journal is replayed before other recovery paths, so an interruption cannot restore an old generation after deletion has begun. Prepared data remains available until verification succeeds.

Inference workers have independent process ownership receipts. Recovery requires verified termination of recorded identities. Legacy active work without trustworthy ownership receipts blocks cleanup; matching command names or PID numbers alone cannot establish ownership. Model downloads and external hosts are outside this local deletion inventory.

Gateway transport observes the matching operation before preparing, purging or releasing a remote target. An accepted remote request stays pending through restart verification. Only matching locally verified status followed by release allows completion. Unreachable targets remain pending, unsupported maintenance endpoints require an upgrade, and reported blocked operations need explicit retry after their cause is resolved. Completed targets are skipped rather than purged again. Execution admission matches paired identity or outbound node and rejects unfinished targets; completed ones supply the new epoch for fresh work.

The offline CLI uses the same local recovery owner without starting the app or contacting Gateways. It records paired remote identities for later reconciliation. A successful local exit does not imply remote completion; the journal can remain partial until those targets return.

Publication and snapshot implementation boundaries

Immutable roots and contention recovery

Persistent containers keep old snapshots stable while keyed writes share unchanged trie paths. DomainRoot partitions a shard by domain so a native checkpoint can iterate native cells without scanning unrelated domains. PersistentKeys stores derived primary-key membership and its estimated memory charge. The hub must freeze values before placing them in these containers: an immutable map does not make an embedded mutable object safe.

Contention recovery retries pure transaction preparation against fresh roots. Generated record identifiers remain stable across retries. After four dependency conflicts, if attempts remain, it requests a five-second reservation for the observed keys. Reservations are FIFO among overlapping requests; disjoint writers and immutable readers can continue. New dependencies relinquish the grant and require reacquisition and recomputation, without extending the ticket's original deadline.

The queue mutex is released before shard/publication locking. Publication rechecks the lease after preparing replacement roots. Expiry revokes permission without interrupting a stalled callback; an expired callback cannot later publish its prepared changes. External execution, network requests and other irreversible side effects do not belong in these retryable callbacks. Exhaustion returns a contention failure with bounded diagnostic facts.

Diagnostics retain 32 recent conflict events and hashes of identities, excluding row values. The separate timing collector accepts at most 32 metric names, each with 128 recent duration samples. Counts and totals are cumulative; its reported recent percentile/max describe only that window. Neither diagnostic view establishes successful execution or durability.

Native file validation and bootstrap

The native codec writes one MessagePack stream across independently checked 256 KiB blocks. A record can cross block boundaries. Large containers and strings/blobs are emitted in chunks with cooperative pacing; this is not hard preemption of every encoder operation. The format represents data, including large signed integers through one defined extension, without executing Python object constructors.

Validation has distinct responsibilities:

Path Evidence required
New snapshot or physical mirror Flush/fsync and complete readback of framing, record identities/deletion flags, footer count, length and digest; the writer validates source rows against trusted schemas.
Reuse of already validated immutable bytes Exact whole-file digest/length, frame structure, accepted catalog header and expected footer; avoids decoding all saved values.
Native bootstrap Complete decoding/migration plus trusted row/group/sequence validation before the repository can become ready.

read() is a lazy iterator: footer and whole-file checks finish only when it is exhausted. Consuming the first few records is not validation of the entire file. The native adapter requires exact row columns, primary keys and group membership, rejects duplicate identities, preserves authoritative tombstones and rebuilds indexes using this process's hash seed. Old hash buckets cannot establish current lookup locations. Obsolete disposable lexical-cache records may be discarded during that rebuild; business records retain their separate validation and migration rules.

An accepted read-only historical catalog is not automatically an allowed export target. Reusing an unchanged domain also requires the current catalog fingerprint and base adapter provenance checks. Creating a valid snapshot file does not select it as the current generation; the checkpoint coordinator owns that publication.

Rebuilding missing storage under a live owner

Storage recovery operates only through the checkpoint writer that still owns live RAM. It verifies the configured parent directory's device/inode identity, real path components, root and repository leases, exact committed manifest and required recovery paths. Missing files can trigger a full rebuild from RAM. Corrupt authority metadata, foreign ownership, symlinks and conflicting file types remain errors; they are not replaced as though they were absent.

Repair recreates private directories and the existing owner's missing lock, then restores retained deletion/cleanup journals before retiring payloads. These journals are independent fences, so their absence cannot mean a deletion finished. Destination identity, manifest authority and saved dependencies are checked again before successful handoff. Health readers use cached writer diagnostics rather than scanning payloads or trying to repair storage themselves.

This live-owner repair differs from startup recovery of a committed generation. It does not load replacement disk data over newer RAM or silently redirect saves when the configured parent mount/path has changed. Recovery after process loss still depends on the last complete selected generation described above.

Explicit offline native conversion

The offline operator also supports optimize and rollback-export, with the same stopped-source ownership and new-destination requirements as copy:

PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m agent_runtime.runtime_state.operator optimize /path/to/hub /path/to/new-hub
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m agent_runtime.runtime_state.operator rollback-export /path/to/hub /path/to/compatibility-hub

Conversion removes disposable derived indexes or reconstructs the old lexical layout for explicit compatibility export. It compares the count and exact encoded digest of authoritative rows, sequences and tombstones before accepting the new file. The legacy exporter reconstructs memberships and 64-entry pages from retained documents/signatures; it is outside the normal live indexing path. Source bytes remain intact, and saved work is never executed to validate a conversion. The output catalog must still be supported by the intended receiving checkout.

Saved model configuration

effective_model pins endpoint/model and internal client settings together with the separate execution_request_overrides, execution_configuration_profile, execution_configuration_version and execution_output_reservation_tokens fields. resume_context carries the equivalent context keys, including llm_execution_request_overrides and llm_execution_configuration_profile. Nested maps are copied so a settings edit cannot mutate stored execution identity.

The saved client profile also pins timeout_seconds, no_actionable_output_timeout_seconds and constrained_recovery_timeout_seconds. Their llm_ context keys travel through admission and resume. Missing historical generation fields default to 90 and 30 seconds; later global changes affect new tasks. This extends the existing checkpoint without a separate migration store.

Recommended profiles are resolved when the selected model is known, then saved as concrete values. Resume and continuation preserve those values instead of recomputing from current recommendations. Legacy snapshots acquire version-0 execution metadata from their saved temperature/output settings and retain the max_tokens wire alias. See Model Configuration and native/state.py.

Durable Memory is separate profile-wide state in agent_memory.db, beside the run database. Its skill owns global JSON keys, indexed tags and CAS revisions. Conversation IDs are provenance only: ordinary deletion retires the owned task/legacy-conversation KV scopes but leaves Memory. Shared task scopes remain with their retained owners. Runs pin only bounded relevant metadata; values require explicit memory.get. See Memory and context.

Monitoring state

The accepted disabled_agent_check_monitoring_enabled boolean is persisted in native state and resume_context and carried into same-task continuations. A recovered run retains its accepted value even after global Settings changes. Legacy states without this field use OFF.

Passive reporting retains at most 128 recent observation identities in diagnostic state. Ordinary trace persistence deduplicates agent_check_observation_id across delivery/reload. No strike, pending approval, completion evidence, model message or execution journal is created by an observation.
